# Basic-condition priority

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Basic-condition priority is independent of C, excludes every natural-number score, and is representable by a bounded score.

`protection-priority-excludes-uniform-aggregation` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F07

Editable record: [protection-priority-excludes-uniform-aggregation.json](protection-priority-excludes-uniform-aggregation.json) · [Register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

Documentary review UTC: `2026-10-08T18:56:05.941008+00:00`. Run the registry checker for source drift; this page is not a fresh proof receipt.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

In one constructed protection-versus-gains situation, living significance, the no-loss generative comparison C and the ordering by basic-condition priority hold together, and basic-condition priority never trades the protected basic condition for any number of secondary gains. Living significance constrains positive relevance, not ordering: it holds equally alongside a trading ordering satisfying C, so basic-condition priority does not follow from C. Every natural-number score satisfying C trades at score 0 + 2 gains, so no such score represents basic-condition priority. A bounded rational score (1 for protection, k/(k+1) for k gains) agrees with basic-condition priority on every pair of options. The situation therefore separates basic-condition priority from unit-step aggregation only.

Canonical source: [ScoreRepresentation.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ScoreRepresentation.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- A single situation: option 0 retains the basic condition with no gain; option k>0 loses it and realizes k generative gains. The basic condition is not counted as new generative content.
- C is GenerativeComparison.ComparisonPrinciple; J2 is PracticalJudgment.Better; G0 is used only to recognize gains as positively relevant. That J2 does not follow from C instances the existing result that C is silent on trade-offs (tradeoff_has_opposite_strict_appraisals, loss_sensitivity_alone_supplies_no_cutoff).

That the protected condition is basic and each gain is generative content realized in the same history requires correspondence E and a classification argument; options are continuations of one history, not holdings of independent owners.

<a id="检验与边界-validation-and-boundaries"></a>
## Validation and boundaries

Successful Lean 4.29.1 check (run 20261008T192627.406862Z): ProtectionPriorityRival 15 theorems/25 declaration audits (11 with no dependency, 1 propext, 5 propext and Quot.sound, 8 also Classical.choice); no custom axiom, sorry or native_decide; same receipt and controls as RenewingFormation. An independent review on 9 October accepted the first version (10 theorems) with corrections; the renames, livingSignificance_leaves_ordering_open and the bounded-score theorems are Lean-checked, but the reviewer did not re-review the corrected version; see GENERATIVE-DISCRIMINATION-REVIEW.

Checks one constructed situation; what it excludes is natural-number (unit-step) scores, not aggregation in general. It does not show that J2 is right elsewhere, that the protected condition is basic, or that bounded-sensitivity rivals fail; in this situation the two cannot be told apart. The record ID's "uniform aggregation" means unit-step aggregation.

- weighted 0 satisfies C yet trades the basic condition for one gain: C does not yield basic-condition priority. [ProtectionPriorityRival.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/universal-ethics/generative-capacity/ProtectionPriorityRival.lean)
- The bounded rational score k/(k+1) agrees with basic-condition priority on every pair in this situation (ratio_agrees_with_priority): bounded-sensitivity rivals are not excluded and remain substantive. [ProtectionPriorityRival.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/universal-ethics/generative-capacity/ProtectionPriorityRival.lean)

Construct situations (several basic conditions, varying stakes) that separate basic-condition priority from bounded-sensitivity scores, or show why none can; extend rival discrimination across situations.
